exposure: Large-volume packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion (>= 4 units within 24 hours postpartum)
Blood conservation strategies (uterine balloon tamponade, embolization, tranexamic acid administration)
cohort: All parturients who received packed red blood cell transfusions between 2016 and 2022 at a class A tertiary general hospital.
finding: Parturients receiving large-volume pRBC transfusions (>= 4 units) had a higher prevalence of previous cesarean delivery and abortion, a history of placenta previa/accreta and placental adhesion, and greater incidences of thrombocytopenia and hypofibrinogenemia, along with longer hospital and ICU stays.
mod_finding: Women with large-volume pRBC transfusions had a greater prevalence of previous cesarean delivery compared to those receiving smaller volumes.
